solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Panting to get hold of riches, for a start?

definitions.text: Panting to get hold of riches, for a start?

indicators.note: getting hold of something means clasping it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: panting is gasping for breath

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the word riches

explanation.surface: Someone is breathless with eagerness to lay hands on wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get hold of' puts R, the start of 'riches', inside GASPING. The whole clue also describes a greedy person, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being greedy and eager to seize wealth is exactly what grasping describes.

clue.text: Climbing hill, Yank gets tummy trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters go upward, read backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
to yank is to tug

explanation.surface: An American hillwalker gets a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb TUG. 'Climbing' turns TOR plus TUG upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutrot is slang for an upset stomach (and for cheap, rough alcohol that causes one).

clue.text: Genoa perhaps is under a second attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts this piece below the others

parts.note: a genoa is a large jib, a type of sail

explanation.surface: The Italian city of Genoa comes under a second assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genoa' looks like the Italian city but is a type of jib sail.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Former investment in opera? Sadly, not a sausage

parts.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a UK investment replaced in 1999

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters being put into a sorry, jumbled state
not a means the letter A is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: An old investment in opera brought no return at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a sausage' is British slang for nothing at all; here 'Sadly' jumbles IN OPERA and 'not' removes its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American dry sausage, an example of the type.

clue.text: No love, not a man to inhale fresh air of the country

indicators.note: no means the following letter is left out
fresh means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A rejected lover goes off into the country to breathe clean air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges NOT A MAN TO INHALE, and 'No love' removes one O. 'air' is a tune, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's official song, its tune or air, is the anthem played on state occasions.

clue.text: Capital changes hands for dog

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so the right-hand letter swaps for the left-hand one

parts.note: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A city or a sum of money is transferred between owners, all on account of a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in PRAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to pester or torment them persistently, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In vexation I pull up plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
In means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Frustrated, someone tears a plant out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the hidden letters NIPUL upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a flowering garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers.

clue.text: Frenchman's held up by drab vegetation

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: drab means grey and dull

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the name is read bottom to top

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is delayed by dull plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up by' reads as delayed, but 'up' reverses the Frenchman's name in this down clue, and 'held' puts that inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage or plants collectively, so vegetation.

clue.text: Wind section's opening note coming in too soon

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so those letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: early means before the expected time

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of section

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: In an orchestra, the wind section's first note comes in prematurely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind section' looks like woodwind players, but 'Wind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: In two senses, a feature of The Times?

definitions.text: In two senses, a feature of The Times?

parts.words: In two senses, a feature of The Times
parts.note: an editorial in the newspaper, and also the word The, which leads its title and is grammatically a definite article

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like description of something in a famous London newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times's main editorial is its leading article, and 'The' at the start of its name is an article that leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article is a newspaper's principal editorial opinion piece, and 'The' is literally a leading grammatical article.

clue.text: Drunkard covers another's back

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: tops are lids or covers
another drunkard, i.e. a sot

explanation.surface: A drunk is protecting a fellow drinker, perhaps literally covering his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another drunkard: SOT. TOPS plus SOT read 'back' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a heavy drinker, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Powerful woman is seducer but no tease, we hear

indicators.note: no means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: a temptress is a woman who seduces

indicators.note: we hear signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: the word tease is pronounced like the plural of the letter T

explanation.surface: A powerful woman is a seducer but not a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tease' said aloud is 'Ts', so 'no tease' removes both Ts from TEMPTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female ruler, a woman with great power.

clue.text: Old climber is sheepish

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: An elderly mountaineer looks embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant. 'sheepish' is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, so it is sheepish in the literal sense of sheep-like.

clue.text: Religious practice, one adopted by the big guns

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the guns hold the numeral

parts.note: ordnance is artillery, the big guns
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A church ritual has been taken up by the powerful people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the big guns' looks like important people, but it means artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance can be a prescribed religious rite or ceremony, such as a sacrament.

clue.text: Yours truly feeds sick rural man on IV, perhaps

indicators.note: feeding something puts it inside, so one piece goes into the other
sick means the letters are in a poor, disordered state

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, i.e. me

explanation.surface: A hospital patient from the countryside is fed by drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges RURAL MAN ON, and 'feeds' puts ME inside. IV looks like an intravenous drip but is the number four.
explanation.definitionFit: IV is how four is written in the Romans' number system, one example of such a figure.

clue.text: Very trivial cryptic clue requiring less up top

indicators.note: in a down clue, up top places this piece first, above the other

parts.note: less means minus, as in subtraction

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are disguised by rearranging

explanation.surface: A trivial crossword clue needing less thought at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUE to CULE, with MINUS 'up top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule means tiny, so of very little importance.

clue.text: Can your setter keep Conservative sweet?

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: can I, your setter, do it? becomes am I able

explanation.surface: The setter wonders if he can keep a Tory friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can your setter' is the question 'Am I able?', AMIABLE, which keeps C.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and good-natured, close to sweet in temperament.

clue.text: French writer of fine novel La Brute

parts.note: F is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A French author wrote a fine novel called La Brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals rearranging LA BRUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Flaubert was the French novelist who wrote Madame Bovary.

clue.text: Soup Ingmar regularly sampled in island port

indicators.note: the sampled letters sit in the middle of the island and the wine

parts.note: Mull is a Scottish island
tawny is a style of port wine

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the name Ingmar

explanation.surface: Ingmar keeps tasting soup in a harbour town on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but is the wine, TAWNY port. Mull is an island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spicy curried soup of Anglo-Indian origin.

clue.text: Refined crude oil is stored in part by European

indicators.note: stored in means kept inside, so these letters go inside
crude means raw and unrefined, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A European keeps some crude oil that has been refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined' and 'crude oil' suggest petroleum, but 'Refined' is the definition and 'crude' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite means well-mannered and cultivated, which is what refined means of a person.

clue.text: Shout about the woman's virginity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to cry is to shout
her refers to the woman

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about a woman's virginity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is slang for virginity, as in losing one's cherry.

clue.text: Political upheaval in Cuba's capital shown by up-to-date broadcast

indicators.note: capital means the leading letter of the word Cuba's
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolution in Havana is covered by the latest news reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests news but signals rearranging UP-TO-DATE; 'Cuba's capital' is its first letter C, not Havana.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden seizure of government power, a violent political upheaval.

clue.text: Germany's crack tenor

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A German singer is a first-rate tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks like a singer but means general meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general sense or gist, as is its tenor.

clue.text: Son's reluctant to become tree-climber

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: A boy is unwilling to grow up into someone who climbs trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth is a slow-moving South American mammal that lives hanging in trees.

clue.text: Social gathering's first to honour Alberich's hairdo

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work and socialising, like a sewing bee

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of honour

parts.note: Alberich is the setter, so Alberich's means the setter has: I've

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a hairstyle that won first prize at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alberich's' is the setter speaking: Alberich has, i.e. I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is a tall, rounded women's hairstyle popular in the 1960s.

clue.text: Tour guide indicates font

definitions.meaning: a person employed to look after travellers on a package holiday

explanation.surface: A tourist guide is pointing at a church fountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier escorts tour groups, and Courier is also a well-known monospaced typeface.

clue.text: One who made will primarily disposed of … this?

definitions.text: One who made will primarily disposed of … this?

indicators.note: the first letter is thrown away

parts.note: a testate is a person who has died leaving a valid will

explanation.surface: A will-maker's chief disposal: this is what the will hands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily disposed of' removes the opening T of TESTATE. Read whole, the clue describes the property a will distributes.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is the property and possessions a person leaves at death, which the will disposes of.

clue.text: Minute exotic tree planted in church yard — or churchyard?

indicators.note: planted in puts the pieces inside, as a tree goes in the ground

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny foreign tree is planted in the churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' makes ETER from TREE; M and ETER are 'planted in' CE ... Y, church and yard written apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchyard is the burial ground round a church, which is a cemetery.
